items.stem: A single vague query returns weak results for a multi-part question. What does agentic retrieval do differently?

options.text: It decomposes the question into focused sub-queries and can use prior results to refine
options.rationale: Correct: planning and sub-query decomposition target each part of the question.

options.text: It simply returns more chunks for the same query
options.rationale: Returning more chunks is not query planning.

options.text: It removes the need for any retrieval
options.rationale: Agentic RAG still retrieves; it plans the retrieval.
It improves targeting but does not guarantee correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: planning and sub-query decomposition target each part of the question.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO controls keep a multi-step research agent safe to run? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a budget bounds cost and prevents runaway execution.

options.text: A termination condition that stops when the question is answered
options.rationale: Correct: a clear stop condition avoids endless loops.

options.text: No limit on the number of retrieval steps
options.rationale: Unbounded steps risk infinite loops and cost blowups.
Intermediate steps must be inspectable to debug the workflow.

items.explanation: Correct: a budget bounds cost and prevents runaway execution.

items.stem: When combining evidence across multiple retrieval steps, why track which step each piece of evidence came from?

options.text: So the final answer can be grounded and the trace reviewed for errors
options.rationale: Correct: provenance across steps supports grounding and debugging.

options.text: Because evidence from later steps is always better
options.rationale: Later steps are not inherently better.

options.text: To make the workflow run faster
options.rationale: Tracking provenance is about grounding, not speed.

options.text: It is unnecessary once an answer is produced
options.rationale: Provenance is exactly what lets you verify the answer.

items.explanation: Correct: provenance across steps supports grounding and debugging.
